analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page explains weight as gravitational field force distinct from aerodynamic forces, states Newton inverse square law, defines g at earth surface and derives W equals m times g, then works an airplane example showing small weight loss with altitude.

overview.headline: Weight as gravity force and its slight decrease with height

keyPoints.point: Weight is a force from gravitational attraction of earth on an object
keyPoints.quote: Weight is the force generated by the gravitational attraction of the earth on any object.

keyPoints.point: Gravitational field force needs no physical contact while aerodynamic mechanical forces do
keyPoints.quote: The gravitational force is a field force; the source of the force does not have to be in physical contact with the object to generate a force.

keyPoints.point: Newton published theory of gravitation with laws of motion in 1686
keyPoints.quote: Newton published his theory of gravitation with his laws of motion in 1686.

keyPoints.point: On earth surface its value is 9.8 meters per square second for gravitational acceleration
keyPoints.quote: On the surface of the earth, its value is 9.8 meters per square second or 32.2 feet per square second.

keyPoints.point: An airplane flying at 35000 feet is about 4007 miles from center of earth
keyPoints.quote: If an airplane is flying at 35000 feet (about 7 miles) the distance to the center of the earth is about 4007 miles.

keyTerms.gloss: force from gravitational attraction that pulls object toward earth
keyTerms.quote: Weight is the force generated by the gravitational attraction of the earth on any object.

keyTerms.gloss: gravitational force acting without physical contact between source and object
keyTerms.quote: The gravitational force is a field force; the source of the force does not have to be in physical contact with the object to generate a force.

keyTerms.gloss: fixed number G used to calculate gravitational force between particles
keyTerms.quote: The gravitational force, F, between two particles equals a universal constant, G, times the product of the mass of the particles

keyTerms.gloss: acceleration from gravity that links mass to weight
keyTerms.quote: The weight W, or gravitational force, is then just the mass of an object times the gravitational acceleration.

keyTerms.gloss: height above surface where weight would decrease
keyTerms.quote: we would expect that the weight of an object would decrease with altitude.

keyTerms.gloss: forces needing physical contact with air to generate effect
keyTerms.quote: Aerodynamic forces are mechanical forces and the object has to be in physical contact with the air which generates the force.
